subject: Subprocessor rollforward: consent tracking & MSA/Order Form redlines
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@atlascloud.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor rollforward: consent tracking & MSA/Order Form redlines

Jordan —

Following our call yesterday, attaching the proposed Annex A (subprocessor schedule) and a short redline of the Order Form that reflects the flow-down language Atlas requested. Key asks from our side: a) confirmation that third-party vendors listed in Annex A will sign the DPA addendum or equivalent flow-down, and b) an expected timeline for SOC2 evidence or attestation from each subprocessor.

I've included a draft consent-tracking spreadsheet (Annex A) that maps each subproc to the data types and the proposed retention windows. Can you confirm AtlasCloud can accept the retention windows in column C or propose alternatives? We need this to complete legal sign-off on our end by EOW Aug 27 to hit the integration milestone.

Next steps I propose:
- Atlas legal to return Order Form redline + call out any subproc that is non-negotiable for you (if any) by Tue Aug 17.
- Procurement to confirm PO timing concurrently.
- Redwood to route final MSA + Order Form to execs for signatures once Annex A is locked.

Attachments: Annex A - Subproc Schedule.xlsx (spreadsheet), Redwood_OrderForm_redline_v1.pdf

Thanks — let me know if you'd prefer a quick 15-min sync.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@atlascloud.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlascloud.com, legal@atlascloud.com
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor rollforward: consent tracking & MSA/Order Form redlines

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the clear summary. We reviewed the materials and have two immediate notes:

1) DPA flow-down: Atlas legal is comfortable with the language in your redline, but our procurement team requires each named subprocessor to either: (a) sign Atlas's DPA addendum; or (b) provide a SOC2 Type II attestation dated within the last 12 months. We can accept (b) as a temporary alternative while the addendum is routed.

2) Logging & access control: we flagged a line in the Order Form redline about audit logs and access by Atlas. Our security team asked for clarification on scope (admin vs. application logs). Please see inline comments in the attached PDF: AtlasCloud_MSA_redline_08016.pdf — I highlighted the two paragraphs that need more precision.

Procurement note: PO coming from Atlas procurement appears to be on track; estimated maturity is Aug 25 pending final language. Will confirm by Aug 18.

If possible, can we get a short pivot table in Annex A that groups subprocessors by risk tier? That will help our legal triage.

Jordan
Jordan Lee
Senior Counsel — AtlasCloud
jordan.lee@atlascloud.com | +1 617-555-4421

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@atlascloud.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor rollforward: consent tracking & MSA/Order Form redlines

Jordan — thanks for the fast review and the PDF with inline comments.

I attached a revised Annex A that adds a risk-tier column and a short note explaining the retention buckets. See: Annex A - Subproc Schedule.xlsx (updated v2). I also added a suggested precise wording for the audit log clause — see Page 2 of the Order Form redline (we proposed "application-level access logs restricted to Atlas personnel with explicit role-based access and limited to events relating to Atlas-managed tenants"). Happy to adjust language on the access scope if Atlas needs administrative logs as well.

Regarding the DPA addendum vs SOC2: our preference is that subprocessors sign the DPA addendum; practically, many of our smaller infra partners prefer to provide a SOC2 attestation first. To keep the deal moving, we can accept a SOC2 attestation with a 45-day hard deadline to execute the DPA addendum. Can you confirm that schedule works for Atlas procurement for any subprocessors that elect (b)?

Proposed next steps:
- Atlas legal confirms acceptance of the 45-day bridge for SOC2 attestation by Fri Aug 20.
- Procurement confirms PO issuance by Aug 25.
- Redwood to prepare final Order Form once Annex A is signed off.

If you prefer, we can stand up a 20-min legal-to-legal call on Thu Aug 19 to resolve the remaining 2 paragraphs.

—Naomi

On Mon, Aug 16, 2027 at 11:03 Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@atlascloud.com> wrote:
> Thanks Naomi — appreciate the clear summary. We reviewed the materials and have two immediate notes:...

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Aug 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: recommendation on subproc approvals (no external recipients)

Naomi / Neha — quick internal note before we reply to Atlas. My read: Accept the 45-day SOC2 bridge for smaller subprocessors but require affirmative evidence (signed attestation PDF uploaded to our drive) and a compliance gating checklist before we enable them to process customer data. For anything Tier 1 (anything storing raw PII or telemetry traces) we should require the DPA addendum upfront.

Operational asks if we accept the bridge:
- Legal to capture the 45-day bridge language in the Order Form (explicit expiration / auto-escalation to DPA).
- Solutions (Lauren) to flag any integrator vendors in Annex A that we should block from production until DPA signed.
- Sales (Naomi) to push procurement for PO timeline; we can't go live without procurement in prod environment.

If there are no objections by EOD Aug 22 I will mark the internal approval path and draft the short contract language.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@atlascloud.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@atlascloud.com, legal@atlascloud.com
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2027 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor rollforward: consent tracking & MSA/Order Form redlines

Naomi —

Quick update after procurement and legal sync: procurement will issue the PO on Aug 30 (subject to the final Order Form attach). Atlas legal confirmed the 45-day SOC2 bridge is acceptable for subprocessors categorized as Tier 2/3. For Tier 1 subprocessors we will require the DPA addendum signed prior to onset.

Per your ask, our vendor operations team will provide SOC2 attestations for the three third-party analytics partners listed in Annex A within 14 days and they are willing to sign the DPA addendum thereafter. Attached is the signed DPA Addendum from Atlas for Redwood to countersign (attached: Signed_DPA_Addendum.pdf).

We should be able to finalize language and move to signatures next week. If you want, schedule the exec-sign page for Tue Sep 1 so we can route quickly.

Jordan
Jordan Lee
Senior Counsel — AtlasCloud
